answer: Saturation is tumbling-window yield of new source_ids below 0.125 for 4 consecutive windows of 8 effort units. On a 12-source seeded corpus (seed 28312) the detector fired at effort 64 after yield collapsed (last new source at 27, discovered 12/12, coverage 1.0000). A still-yielding sequential stream stayed silent (400/400 new sources, yield=1.0 every window). Across 40 trials mean fire_effort was 6:51.6 < 12:70.0 < 24:108.6 (Cohen's d n24 vs n6 = 3.6845, 95% CI on n12 fire_effort [66.8, 73.4]). The OR `evidence_saturation == true OR time_minutes >= 180` logs time_budget distinctly from evidence_saturation; a silent detector plus time_minutes>=180 is detector_silent_at_timeout, never a saturation claim. SUCCESS:TST-0283

implementation.mechanism: Seeded finite corpora are sampled with replacement (coupon collector). Marginal yield is new independent source_ids in a tumbling window of 8. Saturation fires when yield < 0.125 for 4 consecutive windows. evaluate_stopping logs saturation_arm and time_arm separately so time_minutes>=180 cannot relabel a silent detector as saturated.

effect_size.interpretation: Larger true source count must delay fire_effort. Cohen's d for n24 vs n6 mean fire_effort; 0.8 is the large-effect floor.

trial_summary.pass_rule: All trials fire; none premature (coverage<0.75); mean coverage >=0.90; mean fire_effort increases 6<12<24; Cohen's d (n24-n6) >= 0.8. Bootstrap 95% CIs are on the trial means.
